title: Service Discovery, API Gateway & Load Balancing

scenes.heading: Service Discovery, API Gateway & Load Balancing
scenes.narration: Let's see how a fleet of ephemeral instances that scale, crash, and move IPs can behave like one addressable, resilient service.

scenes.heading: Finding services in a moving system
items: Instances come and go, so addresses can't be hardcoded
A registry tracks which instances are alive
Health checks prune the dead; load balancing spreads the rest
scenes.narration: In a microservice system, instances constantly scale, crash, and change IPs, so services can't hardcode each other's addresses. Service discovery solves how they find each other. A registry, like Consul, etcd, or Kubernetes DNS, tracks which instances are alive. Health checks prune the dead ones, and load balancing spreads traffic across the survivors. Once you see discovery as name-to-live-set, the whole topology clicks.

scenes.heading: The discovery lifecycle
steps: Instance starts and registers its address
It heartbeats, or exposes a health endpoint
A reaper deregisters instances that fail checks
Caller resolves the name to live instances
A balancer picks one instance per request
scenes.narration: The lifecycle runs like this. A service starts and registers its address, either itself or via a controller like Kubernetes watching pods. It then heartbeats or exposes a health endpoint, and a reaper continuously deregisters any instance that fails its check, so stale entries don't black-hole traffic. When a caller needs the service, it resolves the name into the live set, and a load-balancing policy such as round-robin picks one instance per request.

scenes.heading: Client-side load balancing
scenes.narration: This is client-side load balancing. Instead of dialing a proxy, the client resolves all live instances from the registry and picks one itself, saving a network hop and giving fine-grained policy. The counter is incremented atomically so concurrent callers stay evenly balanced across backends. gRPC has this built in through a resolver plus a round-robin balancer, which avoids the connection-pinning that plagues naive proxies with long-lived HTTP/2 connections.

scenes.text: The gateway guards client-to-system traffic; the service mesh governs service-to-service traffic.
scenes.narration: Two more pieces sit on top. An API gateway is the single front door for clients: it routes, terminates TLS, authenticates, rate-limits, and can aggregate several backend calls into one response. A service mesh pushes discovery, mutual TLS, retries, and traffic policy into sidecar proxies on every pod. The gateway guards north-south, client-to-system traffic, while the mesh governs east-west, service-to-service traffic.

scenes.text: Registry + health checks + load balancing turn ephemeral instances into one self-healing, addressable service.
scenes.narration: Put together, a registry with health checks and load balancing turns a set of ephemeral instances into a self-healing, addressable service, while gateways and meshes externalize cross-cutting networking out of your Go code. That's what lets a system auto-scale and survive crashes without callers ever noticing.
